html:
SMTO-LLM-0016 — The model stopped making progress on its reply

GUID: 891e9eda-1fc7-4e99-9169-4edab2b72d5c
Slug: model-generation-stalled-no-action
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: provider

What happened

  • The model went quiet partway through its reply and sent nothing useful for the allowed time (5 minutes by default). SMTO stopped waiting and didn't carry out any part of that reply.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing, open the Main card, and select Check saved model. A model server that is overloaded or frozen stops sending progress, and this test shows whether it is answering.
  2. If your model is just slow, open Limits and recovery on the Main card, raise No-output timeout (or Recovery timeout if SMTO was retrying a step), and select Save Main. Only these two settings control how long SMTO waits without progress; other timeouts won't change this.
  3. If you raised a timeout, ask SMTO to continue in a new message. If not, on the stopped task, select Resume (or Continue task if that is what it shows). A resumed task keeps the timeout it started with, while new work uses the new value; finished steps stay done either way.

What success looks like

  • The model keeps sending progress and the reply finishes without this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the model server; the server may be overloaded or stuck. When you continue in a new message, say which steps are already done so nothing is repeated.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • After generation started, no meaningful reasoning, answer text, tool-argument text or increasing generation counter arrived within the configured inactivity allowance (model_generation_stalled_no_action).

What this means

  • The generation inactivity timer expired since the last meaningful progress. New reasoning resets this timer. Heartbeats, whitespace and unchanged counters do not. This does not establish the underlying provider failure.

Why this can happen

  • No meaningful generation progress arrived within the configured inactivity allowance.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the inactivity duration and threshold. New reasoning and increasing generation counters count as progress.

How to fix it

  • Compare duration_seconds and threshold_seconds in provider_diagnostic with provider load and logs. If the provider is legitimately slow, raise the role's No-output timeout (llm_no_actionable_output_timeout_seconds) or, during recovery, Recovery timeout (llm_constrained_recovery_timeout_seconds), both 300 s by default, in Settings › Setup › Model routing; changes apply to new tasks and resumed tasks keep their saved values. Don't change unrelated timeouts or budgets.
  • Check Generation inactivity timeout or Recovery inactivity timeout in Model Configuration. Both default to 300 seconds. Increase the applicable allowance for a slow provider. Prior completed work is preserved.

Relevant SMTO settings

  • Open Generation Inactivity Timeout: model-configuration / llm_no_actionable_output_timeout_seconds. Applies to: new task.
  • Start a new task after changing this setting. Active and resumed tasks retain their captured values.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • Observable generation progresses within the inactivity allowance.

What not to do

  • Do not change an unrelated timeout, budget or policy. Check whether the named setting applies only to a new task.

Technical notes

  • The current decision is rejected before tool authorization when enforcement applies; earlier results are not replayed.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
